paper_title: Exploration of the polarization angle variability of the Crab Nebula with POLARBEAR and its application to the search for axion-like particles
suggested_experiment_name: POLARBEAR Tau A polarization oscillation search
coupling_convention: g_agamma in GeV^-1, canonical axion-photon coupling
notes: Paper reports median 95% upper bound on ALP-photon coupling g_agamma < 2.16×10^-12 GeV^-1 × (m_a/10^-21 eV) over mass range 9.9×10^-23 eV to 7.7×10^-19 eV. This is a mass-dependent bound with linear scaling in mass. The bound is derived from polarization angle oscillation measurements of the Crab Nebula (Tau A) using POLARBEAR 150 GHz observations from 2015-2016. The paper assumes the ALP field is stochastic and Gaussian, and that ALPs constitute all local dark matter with density ρ_DM = 0.3 GeV/cm^3. A hint of signal at 2.5σ was found but interpreted conservatively as upper limit.
